correctness.rationale: The weighted transport norm identity is exact and yields the minimum modulus \(\exp(m_a(t))\). Superadditivity implies the sharp uniform exponential rate. Monotone convergence proves the kinematic criterion. If every fixed-length least mass is zero, normalized broad support bumps produce generator residual ratios tending to zero for every finite \(p\ge1\) on the exact domain. Huynh Theorem 3.6 therefore forbids positive expansiveness. A positive least mass at some window length gives uniform exponential expansion and an explicit coercivity estimate by the generator-displacement identity; Huynh Theorem 4.2 implies positive expansiveness. Direct integration proves both examples. No finite computation is used as infinite proof. Sources: arXiv:2611.01005, Theorems 3.3, 3.6, 4.2.

value.rationale: Complete every finite-exponent and all-bounded-nonnegative-potential classification of three natural semigroup growth/expansiveness properties for a non-surjective class. The structural generator coercivity versus approximate-null alternative is new mathematical content needed to bridge abstract criteria and concrete transport weights. The endpoint lower-growth exponent is computed exactly and shown not always attained; explicit logarithmic weights produce a strict kinematic/positive separation. Motivated by the 2026 problem of distinguishing reparametrization expansiveness from orbit growth.
